standfirst: This issue covers Anthropic's move to open up Agent Skills, large ChatGPT Work rollouts, falling LLM prices and a set of skills you can try.
digest: There were no big model launches this week; the news is about standards and rollouts. Anthropic donated the Agent Skills format to the Agentic AI Foundation, with more than 70 platforms already supporting it, and OpenAI released a Decisions API for fast, low-cost calls.

For a consultant, the practical point is that skills are becoming portable. A skill written for Claude is more likely to work in tools your clients already use, so building a small library of them is a safer bet than it was a month ago.

Two enterprise stories show what adoption looks like. Uber is rolling ChatGPT Work out to more than 30,000 staff, and a restaurant franchisee cut cash reconciliation time by 94%. Use them as reference points for large and small clients.

Price is the other client question. A widely discussed post looks at why OpenAI and Anthropic cut prices by up to 80% within months, and IBM's CEO argues open-weight models are now cheap and good enough to run on-premises.

To try this week: Hallmark for less generic design, Claude SEO for marketing audits, and VoiceStudio for local transcription and dubbing. Claude Code 2.1.309 also fixes sandbox gaps, which matters for security-minded clients.

items.title: Anthropic donates the Agent Skills standard to the Agentic AI Foundation
items.summary: Skills, the format behind Claude's reusable instructions, now sit with a foundation, and more than 70 platforms including ChatGPT and Copilot support it.

items.title: OpenAI's Decisions API targets fast, low-cost calls inside apps
items.summary: Fast, cheap, narrowly scoped model calls for applications. Mostly for builders, but useful to know when a client asks about running costs.

items.title: Uber rolls ChatGPT Work out to more than 30,000 employees
items.summary: Teams use it for research, data analysis and presentations. A large-company rollout reference for clients asking how enterprise adoption looks in practice.

items.title: Franchisee cuts cash reconciliation time by 94% with ChatGPT Work
items.summary: A restaurant franchisee built a workflow for cash reconciliation and menu repricing, saving most of the time. A small-business example for finance clients.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.309 fixes sandbox gaps on macOS and Linux
items.summary: Shell startup files no longer run outside the sandbox, and symlinked folders now respect write restrictions. Update if your team uses sandboxed commands.

sections.title: Tools and skills you can use

items.title: Hallmark is a Claude Code skill against generic AI design
items.summary: A skill that steers Claude Code, Cursor and Codex away from templated-looking pages. Useful when you build client mock-ups. Worth an afternoon.

items.title: Claude SEO adds 26 SEO sub-skills to Claude Code
items.summary: Covers technical SEO, schema, local and e-commerce audits and PDF or Excel reports. Handy for marketing clients, though live data needs optional extensions.

items.title: VoiceStudio runs voice cloning, dubbing and transcription locally
items.summary: An open-source, local alternative to ElevenLabs for dubbing, dictation, transcription and audiobooks. Useful for meeting notes and client videos; expect a download and setup.

items.title: Open SEO is an open-source alternative to Semrush and Ahrefs
items.summary: Aims to replace paid SEO suites. Compare it against a client's current tool before suggesting a switch.

items.title: Claude-mem carries context between Claude Code sessions
items.summary: Records what the agent does, compresses it and feeds the relevant parts into later sessions. Helps on long client projects where you keep re-explaining background.

items.title: Video-use lets coding agents edit videos for you
items.summary: From the browser-use team: describe the edit and an agent such as Claude Code does it. Fits quick client demo clips; some setup likely.

items.title: Garry Tan shares his Claude Code setup as 23 tools
items.summary: Role-based tools for design, QA, release and docs work. Worth a look to see how one experienced user structures Claude Code.

items.title: Anthropic guide says most agents need fewer subagents
items.summary: Anthropic's Oct 22 guide favours one main loop with skills and tool search. Claude Code's system prompt was cut by over 80%.

items.title: Why OpenAI and Anthropic cut LLM prices by up to 80%
items.summary: A blog post on how prices fell within months and what drove it, with a busy Hacker News discussion. Handy background for client cost conversations.

items.title: IBM's CEO says open-weight models now work well on-premises
items.summary: The Register reports IBM's view that open-weight models are good and cheap enough to run in-house. Relevant for clients with strict data rules.

items.title: Context engineering: where the practice stands now
items.summary: An overview of how teams manage what a model sees, popular on Hacker News. Useful vocabulary for client agent conversations.

items.title: Builder uses Claude Code to give a pizzeria its own ordering app
items.summary: The first paying customer is live. Claude Code wrote the app, back-end functions and payments, so regulars avoid 30% delivery fees.
